correctness.rationale: A left vertex in color i earns b−y_i and is a best responder only at minimum y; similarly right is optimal only at minimum x. A missing color on either side forces disjoint supports, while full supports force uniform x_i=a/q and y_i=b/q. In a uniform mixed profile, simultaneous strict gains for two players require a cross-part different-color swap, uniquely yielding +1 each; all proper profiles already maximize every payoff individually. Disjoint-support labeled counts use Stirling surjections and the mixed class balanced multinomial. Independent brute force checked 6 parameter triples, including K3,3 q3 with 42 proper and 36 mixed; source program for broader bounded census inspected. Infinite result derives from exact inequalities.

value.rationale: It identifies a natural network family where resistance to just two-agent coalitions certifies full efficiency, with a sharp divisibility obstruction and exact profile census. This structural converse to general one-way coalition-resilience statements can be used directly in stability calculations.

final_claim: For all a,b>=1 and q>=2, all pure Nash equilibria of unweighted complete-bipartite max-q-cut games are either proper support-disjoint optimal/strong colorings or equal-frequency full-support profiles when q|a,b; the latter admit exactly ab(1−1/q) cross-part profitable color-swap pairs, so 2-strong=strong=optimal, with exact labeled counts and PoA q/(q−1) iff divisibility.
